newsitem.title: USA: Dana to sell Berwick manufacturing assets.
newsitem.headline: Dana to sell Berwick manufacturing assets.

text.p: Dana Corp said Monday it would sell the manufacturing assets of a leaf spring manufacturing operation as part of a strategy to focus on its core business units.
Dana said in a statement it had signed an agreement to sell the Berwick, Pa., assets to Hendrickson International Corp of Woodridge, Illinois.
A company spokesman declined to disclose the sale price but said the plant had about $14 million in sales in 1996.
The facility, which makes springs for the U.S. heavy truck and trailer market, will close later this year as a result.
Dana said it charged the closing -- an estimated after-tax cost of $5.3 million, or $0.05 a share -- to earnings during the second quarter.
It added that it would assist the plant's 96 employees in finding other work.

"The sale is the latest in a series of strategic moves in 1997 that has included Dana's planned acquisition of Eaton Corp's global axle and brake operations, as well as the purchase of Clark-Hurth Components and the cylinder liner and piston ring operations of SPX Corp," it said.
"Dana also divested its European warehouse distribution facilities and has announced the sale of its global clutch and hydraulic cylinder operations," it added.
Dana's core businesses are axles, driveshafts, structural components (frames), sealing products, filtration products, engine products, industrial products and leasing services.
Hendrickson is a subsidiary of the privately-held Boler Co of Itasca, Ill. It specializes in the manufacture of heavy truck and tractor trailer lift and fixed-air suspensions.
